What is creative intelligence for mobile user acquisition? A complete guide
Tomas Hubka
Last updated: Sep 02, 2026
min read
What is creative intelligence for mobile user acquisition, and how does it work? A complete guide to what it surfaces, why it matters, and how UA and creative teams put it to work.
If you've spent any time optimizing user acquisition in mobile gaming, you already know the answer to the biggest question:
why do some studios keep winning while others plateau?
It rarely comes down to the network, the targeting, or the budget. It comes down to the creative.
A stronger ad hooks the right player faster, converts higher, and reduces the pressure on every other lever in your funnel. A weaker ad forces you to spend more, target broader, and refresh more often to keep results afloat. Creative is the single biggest lever in mobile UA, and creative intelligence is how you pull it.
This guide covers what creative intelligence is, why it's become mission-critical for mobile studios, and how the best UA and creative teams put it to work.
Ad Insights: Creative Intelligence
What is creative intelligence?
Creative intelligence is the practice of studying advertising creatives at scale, in market, in order to understand what's working and why. Instead of guessing which formats, hooks, or visual patterns are driving results, you look at real ads running right now across the games in your genre, analyze how they perform, and extract patterns you can apply to your own campaigns.
It's a subset of the broader
ad intelligence
category, which covers everything from spend estimation to network targeting to campaign structure. Creative intelligence zooms in specifically on the creative asset itself: the video, the playable, the image, the sequencing, the hook, the CTA, the emotional beat.
The best creative intelligence tools don't just show you ads. They let you filter by genre, format, network, region, audience, and performance signal, so you can surface the specific creatives that map to your game and your market. From there, the work is pattern recognition: what do the top performers in your genre have in common? Where are they diverging? Which patterns are emerging? Which are declining?
Answering those questions used to require a large in-house creative research team. Today, tools like
Ad Insights
put the same capability within reach for studios of any size.
How does creative intelligence actually work?
At its core, creative intelligence works by continuously scanning the mobile advertising ecosystem, capturing the ads running across it, and turning that raw stream into a searchable, filterable library that UA and creative teams can act on.
Ad discovery
: Creative intelligence platforms continuously monitor mobile ad networks and public advertising activity across dozens of platforms. When a new creative goes live, it gets captured, tagged, and added to the searchable library, usually within hours of it going live in market.
Enrichment and tagging
: Each captured creative gets enriched with structured metadata such as the advertising game, the studio, the ad network, the countries it's running in, the format (video, playable, image), the CTA, the campaign goal, and the estimated impressions. The best platforms also extract deeper data: video length, hook style, on-screen copy, visual patterns.
Search, filter, and analyze
: The library becomes queryable. UA and creative teams can filter creatives by genre, format, network, region, audience, growth signal, or engagement metrics like reposts and comments. The stronger the filtering, the faster the pattern recognition.
Pattern recognition
: With the right filters applied, patterns emerge fast. Which hooks are winning in casual puzzle right now? Which formats are converting best in Germany? Which studios have started running playables in the past 30 days? These are the questions a good creative intelligence workflow answers in minutes, not weeks.
